about: Numbers law reach group A uses (src/core2/law-reach/group-a*.ts), each tagged SOURCED (with its citation), ESTIMATED (with its source and spread) or TUNABLE (with the spread it's checked against). Turnout costs are in the voting engine's own units: a full work week of scheduled hours is a cost of one (campaign parameter turnoutWorkWeekMinutes).

adultAge.source: U.S. Constitution, 26th Amendment (voting age); age of majority in every state but Alabama, Mississippi and Nebraska.

childAgeBelow.source: Child access prevention laws cover minors under 18 in most states (Giffords Law Center, Child Access Prevention, 2024).

cannabisAge.source: Every state adult-use cannabis law sets 21 as the purchase age (National Conference of State Legislatures, Cannabis Overview, 2024).

concealedCarryAge.source: Most permit states issue concealed carry permits from age 21 (Giffords Law Center, Minimum Age to Purchase and Possess, 2024).

handgunPurchaseAge.source: 18 U.S.C. 922(b)(1): licensed dealers may not sell handguns to anyone under 21; state laws extend the age to private sales.

juvenileCourtAgeBelow.source: Vermont Act 201 of 2018 brought 18-year-olds into juvenile court in 2022; proposals elsewhere go to 20 or 21.

reproductiveAgeFrom.source: CDC National Center for Health Statistics: women of reproductive age, 15 to 44.

reproductiveAgeBelow.source: CDC National Center for Health Statistics: women of reproductive age, 15 to 44.

socialMediaAgeFrom.source: Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (15 U.S.C. 6501): platforms bar users under 13; state age verification laws cover 13 to 17 (Utah SB 152 of 2023).

federalMinimumWageTargetMinor.source: Raise the Wage Act of 2023 (S. 2488, 118th Congress): $17.00 an hour.

stateMinimumWageTargetMinor.source: State and city increases to $15.00 an hour (California, New York, Illinois, New Jersey, Maryland, Massachusetts, Connecticut, Delaware; Economic Policy Institute Minimum Wage Tracker, 2024).

paidLeavePremiumShare.source: 2025 paid family leave payroll premiums: California SDI 1.2% (with disability), Washington 0.92%, Massachusetts 0.88%, New York 0.388%, New Jersey family leave 0.09%; this is a middle value of the family-leave share.

consumerLoanRateCap.source: Military Lending Act, 10 U.S.C. 987: 36% military annual percentage rate; the common state cap (National Consumer Law Center, State Rate Caps, 2024).

pretrialJailShare.source: Bureau of Justice Statistics, Jail Inmates in 2022: 664,000 held in local jails, about 70% not convicted, of 333 million residents.

disenfranchisedShare.source: The Sentencing Project, Locked Out 2024: 4.0 million people, 1.7% of the voting-age population, can't vote because of a felony conviction.

restoredVoterShare.source: The Sentencing Project, Locked Out 2022 and 2024: about half of those disenfranchised have finished their sentences (0.5 of 1.7% of the voting-age population).

photoIdBaseCost.source: GAO-15-19 (2014): strict photo ID lowered turnout 2 to 3 points in Kansas and Tennessee; Cantoni and Pons (Quarterly Journal of Economics, 2021) find a smaller effect. Checked against a 0 to 3 point turnout drop.

photoIdNoWorkCost.source: GAO-15-19 (2014): the drop was largest among young, new and lower-income voters, who less often hold a current license; here it rises as scheduled work falls.

automaticRegistrationRelief.source: Brennan Center for Justice (2019): automatic registration raised registration 9 to 94%; McGhee and Romero (Public Policy Institute of California, 2021) find a turnout gain of about 1 to 3 points among new registrants.

sameDayRegistrationRelief.source: Grumbach and Hill (Journal of Politics, 2022): same-day registration raises turnout among 18 to 24 year olds by about 3 points, and less with age.

sameDayRegistrationAgeSpanYears.source: Grumbach and Hill (2022): the gain shrinks with age and is near zero past middle age; the relief falls to zero over this many years past 18.

mailVotingWorkRelief.source: Gerber, Huber and Hill (Political Science Research and Methods, 2013): all-mail elections in Washington raised turnout about 2 to 4 points; the share of the work-time cost of getting to the polls a mailed ballot removes.

rentIncreaseCap.source: California AB 1482 (5% plus inflation, at most 10%), Oregon SB 608 (7% plus inflation, at most 10% since 2023), St. Paul (3%).

inclusionaryAffordableShare.source: Grounded Solutions Network, Inclusionary Housing Database (2021): the typical set-aside is 10 to 20% of new homes.

housingAssistanceAnnualMinor.source: HUD, Picture of Subsidized Households 2023: the average housing choice voucher pays about $960 a month.

parksDedicatedShare.source: Trust for Public Land, LandVote: dedicated park levies typically add a fifth or more to a city's park spending.

lobbyingCoolingOffYears.source: National Conference of State Legislatures, Revolving Door Prohibitions (2024): most states bar former officials from lobbying for one or two years.

termLimitYears.source: National Conference of State Legislatures, The Term-Limited States (2024): most term-limited legislatures allow 8 years in a chamber; city charters commonly allow two four-year terms.

publicPositionAnnualMinor.source: BLS OEWS May 2023 mean annual wages (correctional officers $59,840, police officers $74,910, firefighters $63,890) plus benefits at 38% of state and local government compensation (BLS Employer Costs for Employee Compensation, 2024): about $100,000 a year per position.

hireAgeBelow.source: Public employers hire working-age adults; the upper age past which a named adult isn't considered for a new public job.

daysPerYear.source: Civil calendar: a common year has 365 days.

minimumWageNextStepShare.source: Where a state's floor already meets the $15 standard, a raise follows the next proposals: California's Proposition 32 (2024) would have raised its $16.00 floor to $18.00, 12.5 percent; Washington and Seattle proposals of 2024 to 2025 ran 10 to 20 percent above their indexed floors. A raise sets the larger of the $15 standard and the floor in force raised by this share, to the nearest quarter.

rightToWorkMembershipPoints.source: Fortin, Lemieux and Lloyd, Right-to-Work Laws, Unionization, and Wage Setting (NBER Working Paper 30098, 2022): union membership falls about 4 percentage points five years after adoption, in an event study of five states.

publicBargainingPayPremium.source: Public-sector union wage differential after controlling for worker characteristics: 3.68 percent (NBER Working Paper 1920); a survey of 75 studies reports 8 to 12 percent without such controls (Cato Institute Research Brief 71), and some quasi-experimental studies find little effect. The value is the conditional estimate rounded up, inside the literature's range.

publicBargainingPhaseYears.source: A first contract takes time to be bargained and phased in; contracts commonly run three years. Spread over those years here.

rightToWorkPhaseYears.source: Fortin, Lemieux and Lloyd (NBER Working Paper 30098, 2022): the effect is measured five years after adoption; it is spread evenly over those years here.
